scope.q: What is the required fidelity of access control enforcement, specifically regarding group-based permissions from each source, and how should conflicts be resolved?
scope.why: Access control is critical for enterprise search to prevent unauthorized data exposure, and reconciling disparate permission models is a complex engineering challenge.

scope.q: Beyond simple keyword search, what advanced query capabilities are essential, e.g., filtering by document type, author, date range, or content within specific channels?
scope.why: This defines the complexity of the search engine and user interface, determining if we need basic full-text search or a more sophisticated faceted search experience.

scope.q: What is the expected real-time latency for new content to become searchable across all sources, especially for ephemeral platforms like Slack where information decay is rapid?
scope.why: Real-time indexing is a significant engineering challenge, particularly across multiple diverse sources, and directly impacts the perceived freshness and utility of search results.

decomposition.title: Source Data Connectors & Ingestion Pipelines
decomposition.why: Each distinct data source (Confluence, Drive, Slack, Wiki) requires a dedicated mechanism to extract, transform, and load its content into a unified system.

decomposition.title: Unified Indexing & Search Engine Core
decomposition.why: A central, optimized index is required to store all ingested data and power fast, relevant search queries across all sources.

decomposition.title: Access Control & Permissions Synchronization
decomposition.why: Ensuring users only see content they are authorized for, consistent with original source permissions, is a fundamental and complex security requirement.

decomposition.title: Search User Interface & API Gateway
decomposition.why: Users need a single, intuitive interface to interact with the search system, backed by a robust API for query processing and result presentation.

decomposition.title: Relevance Ranking & User Feedback Loop
decomposition.why: Initial search results will likely be suboptimal without mechanisms to tune relevance and incorporate user behavior for continuous improvement.

risks.risk: Unforeseen complexities or lack of API access for the 'very old wiki,' making content ingestion difficult or impossible.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize an initial manual export/ingestion for critical wiki content; explore specialized web scraping tools with human oversight for remaining content if no API exists.

risks.risk: Maintaining real-time or near real-time synchronization across all data sources, especially for dynamic platforms like Slack, leading to stale search results.
risks.mitigation: Implement webhook-driven updates for sources supporting them (e.g., Slack); for others, develop robust incremental sync mechanisms with clear refresh intervals and monitoring.

risks.risk: Inconsistent or conflicting access control policies across different source systems, resulting in unauthorized data exposure or blocked legitimate access.
risks.mitigation: Design a centralized permission mapping service; conduct thorough security audits and user acceptance testing with diverse user roles against real data sets.

risks.risk: Poor search relevance due to diverse content formats, lack of metadata, or user query ambiguity, leading to continued user frustration.
risks.mitigation: Implement initial NLP techniques for content enrichment; establish a user feedback mechanism within the UI to collect relevance signals, and track query analytics to identify common search failures.
